summary: Marsh Peak in the Uinta Mountains is listed only as an unknown or undocumented site. No lookout is confirmed; a radio tower's ruins lie south of the summit.

facts.status_note: Listed only as an unknown or undocumented site, not a confirmed lookout.

visit.trail_note: No trail to the summit; a climbing guide says it is easy to climb and can be done in a day.

evidence.supports: Uintah County; the peak is in the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Utah list
the peak is filed under unknown or undocumented sites, not lookouts
such a site would move to the lookout list if evidence showed regular fire-lookout use
evidence.quote: If evidence or documentation is uncovered showing that any of these were actually used as regular wildland fire lookout sites, they will be moved to the lookout lists.

evidence.supports: Marsh is one of the two easternmost 12,000-foot peaks in the Uinta Mountains
evidence.quote: Marsh and Leidy Peaks are the eastern most 12,000 foot peaks in the Uintas

evidence.supports: Marsh Peak is a rounded summit, not very rugged
evidence.quote: are very rounded and not very rugged

evidence.supports: not very rugged apart from an east-facing cirque; seldom climbed; no summit register
evidence.quote: Marsh Peak is not a rugged peak, except for its east facing cirque, but it is very seldom climbed, and there is no register on the summit.
Like all peaks in the Uintas, except for Bald Mountain, Marsh Peak has no trail to the summit.

evidence.supports: easy to climb and can be done in a day
evidence.quote: The peak is still easy to climb, and can be easily done in a day

evidence.supports: ruins of an old helicopter-serviced radio tower south of the summit
evidence.quote: There are however, ruins of an old helicopter serviced radio tower south of the summit.

notes_for_editor: No source read documents a fire lookout on Marsh Peak. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it only as an unknown or undocumented Utah site, so the editor may want to mark it unconfirmed or hide it from the lookout map. The story is short because the only detail is the peak and the ruins of a radio tower. Two web searches and the Ashley National Forest history pages turned up nothing about Marsh Peak as a lookout; the Forest history page names only the Ute Mountain tower. The radio-tower ruins come from a single climbing guide page, which gives no date for them.
